sanskrit: kasminn aṅge tapo asyādhi tiṣṭhati kasminn aṅga ṛtam asyādhyāhitam | kva vrataṃ kva śraddhāsya tiṣṭhati kasminn aṅge satyam asya pratiṣṭhitam ||
english: In which limb does his austerity abide? In which limb is his cosmic order established? Where do his vow and his faith stand? In which limb is his truth firmly founded?

sanskrit: kva brahma kva tiṣṭhanty āpaḥ kasminn aṅge diśo asya pratiṣṭhitāḥ | katamad aṅgam anu saṃ carete ahorātre saṃvidāne samānam ||
english: Where is the sacred power, where do the waters stand? In which limb are the directions established? Along which limb do day and night, in mutual accord, move together as one?

sanskrit: kasminn aṅge tiṣṭhati bhūmir asya kasminn aṅge tiṣṭhaty antarikṣam | kasminn aṅge tiṣṭhaty āhitā dyauḥ kasminn aṅge tiṣṭhaty uttaraṃ divaḥ ||
english: In which limb does his earth stand? In which limb does the atmosphere stand? In which limb is heaven set in place? In which limb stands what is beyond the sky?

sanskrit: kasmād aṅgād dīpyate agnir asya kasmād aṅgāt pavate mātariśvā | kasmād aṅgād vi mimīte 'dhi candramāḥ skambhasya mahad vimimāno aṅgam ||
english: From which limb does his fire blaze? From which limb does Mātariśvan blow? From which limb does the moon measure out, measuring the great limb of the Pillar?

sanskrit: kva prepsan dīpyata ūrdhvo agniḥ kva prepsan pavate mātariśvā | yatra prepsantīr abhiyanty āvṛtaḥ skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: Striving to reach where does fire blaze upward? Striving to reach where does Mātariśvan blow? Where do the encompassing forces approach in their striving? Tell us that Pillar — which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: kva prepsantī yuvatī virūpe ahorātre dravataḥ saṃvidāne | yatra prepsantīr abhiyanty āpaḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Striving to reach where do the two young women of different forms, day and night, run in mutual accord? Where do the waters approach in their striving? — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: kvārdhamāsāḥ kva yanti māsāḥ saṃvatsareṇa saha saṃvidānāḥ | yatra yanty ṛtavo yatrārtavāḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Where do the fortnights go? Where do the months go, in accord together with the year? Where the seasons go, where the seasonal moments go — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yasmin skandhā prajāpatir lokān sarvām̐ adhārayat | skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: He upon whose branches Prajāpati upheld all the worlds — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: yat paramam avamaṃ yac ca madhyamaṃ prajāpatiḥ sasṛje viśvarūpam | kiyatā skambhaḥ pra viveśa tatra yan na pārviśat kva tad babhūva ||
english: What is the highest, what is the lowest, and what is the middle, all-formed — which Prajāpati created — how far did the Pillar enter there? What did not enter it, where did that come to be?

sanskrit: kiyatā skambhaḥ pra viveśa bhūtaṃ kiyad bhaviṣyad anvāśaye 'sya | ekaṃ yad aṅgam akṛṇot sahasradhā kiyatā skambhaḥ pra viveśa tatra ||
english: How far did the Pillar enter into what has come to be? How much of what is yet to be lies latent within it? The one limb that it made thousandfold — how far did the Pillar enter there?

sanskrit: yatra lokāś ca kośāś ca brahma yatra janā viduḥ | asac ca yatra sac cāntaḥ skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: Where the worlds and the treasuries are, where people know the sacred power to be, where non-being and being are within — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: yatra tapaḥ parākramya ṛtaṃ dhārayaty uttaram | vrataṃ ca yatra śraddhā ca brahmāpaḥ samāhitāḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Where austerity, having gone forth beyond, holds up the higher cosmic order; where vow and faith, sacred power and the waters are gathered together — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yasmin bhūmir antarikṣaṃ dyaur asminn adhyāhitā | yatrāgniś candramā sūryo vātas tiṣṭhanty ārpitāḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: In which earth, atmosphere, and heaven are set aloft; where fire, the moon, the sun, and wind stand fixed in place — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yasya trayastriṃśad devā aṅge sarve samāhitāḥ | skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: He in whose limb all thirty-three gods are gathered together — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yatra ṛṣayo bhūtakṛta ṛcaḥ sāma yajur mahī | ekarṣir yasminn ārpitāḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Where the seers who brought things into being, the Ṛc verses, the Sāman, the Yajus, and the great earth — the solitary seer in whom they are all fixed — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yasya catasraḥ pradiśo nāḍyas tiṣṭhanti prapyasāḥ | yajño yasmin parākrāntaḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Whose four directions stand as arteries stretched to their reach; in whom sacrifice has gone forth beyond — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yatrāmṛtaṃ ca mṛtyuś ca puruṣaś ca samāhitāḥ | samudro yasya nāḍyaḥ skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: Where immortality and death and the Person are gathered together; whose arteries are the ocean — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: ye puruṣe brahma vidus te skambham anu saṃ viduḥ | yo veda parameṣṭhinaṃ yaś ca veda prajāpatim | jyeṣṭhaṃ ye brāhmaṇaṃ vidus te skambham anu saṃ viduḥ ||
english: Those who know the sacred power in the Person, they truly know the Pillar. He who knows Parameṣṭhin, and he who knows Prajāpati — those who know the eldest Brahman, they truly know the Pillar.

sanskrit: yasya śiro vaiśvānaraś cakṣur aṅgiraso 'bhavan | aṅgāni yasya yātavaḥ skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: Whose head is Vaiśvānara, whose eyes the Aṅgirases became; whose limbs are the demonic forces — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: yasya brahma mukham āhur jihvāṃ madhukaśām uta | virājaṃ yasyodha āhuḥ skambhaṃ (…) ||
english: Whose mouth they call the sacred word, and whose tongue the honey-whip; whose udder they call the Virāj — [that Pillar, tell us which one precisely it is].

sanskrit: yasmād ṛco apātakṣaṃ yajur yasmād apākaṣan | chandāṃsi yasya lomāni skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: From whom they carved the Ṛc verses, from whom they scraped out the Yajus; whose body-hairs are the metres — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: asacchākhāṃ pratiṣṭhantīṃ paramam iva janā viduḥ | uto san manyante 'vare ye 'sya śākhām upāsate
english: People know the branch of non-being as if it were the highest support; yet those of lesser insight who worship his branch consider it to be being.

sanskrit: yatrādityāś ca rudrāś ca vasavaś ca samāhitāḥ | skambhaṃ taṃ brūhi katamaḥ svid eva saḥ ||
english: Where the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus are gathered together — tell us that Pillar, which one precisely is it?

sanskrit: yasya trayastriṃśad devā nidhiṃ rakṣanti sarvadā | nidhiṃ tam adya ko veda yaṃ devā abhirakṣata ||
english: Whose treasure the thirty-three gods always guard — who today knows that treasure which the gods protect?

sanskrit: yatra devā brahmavido brahma jyeṣṭham upāsate | yo vai ta brāhmaṇo veda taṃ vai brahmavido viduḥ ||
english: Where the gods who know the sacred power worship the eldest Brahman — he who truly knows that Brahman, the knowers of Brahman know him.

sanskrit: bṛhanto nāma te devā asatas pari jajñire | ekaṃ tad aṅgaṃ skambhasya- -asad āhuḥ paro janāḥ ||
english: Those gods named the Bṛhant ones were born from non-being; that one limb of the Pillar, further-knowing people call non-being.

sanskrit: yatra skambhaḥ prajanayan purāṇaṃ vyavartayat | ekaṃ tad aṅgaṃ skambhasya purāṇam anu saṃ viduḥ ||
english: Where the Pillar, bringing forth, set the ancient tradition in motion — that one limb of the Pillar those who follow the ancient way truly know.

sanskrit: yatra trayastriṃśad devā aṅgā gātrāṇi bhejire | tān vai trayastriṃśad devān eke brahmavido viduḥ ||
english: Where the thirty-three gods took their portions as limbs and body-parts — those very thirty-three gods certain knowers of the sacred power truly know.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbhaṃ paramam anatyudyaṃ janā viduḥ | skambhas tad agre prāsiñcad dhiraṇyaṃ loke antarā ||
english: People know the Golden Embryo as the supreme, as the unexcellable risen one; the Pillar poured out that golden light in the beginning, within the world.

sanskrit: skambhe lokāḥ skambhe tapaḥ skambhe 'dhy ṛtam āhitam | skambhaṃ tvā vidma pratyakṣam indre sarvaṃ samāhitam ||
english: In the Pillar are the worlds; in the Pillar is austerity; upon the Pillar is cosmic order established. We know you, the Pillar, directly — in Indra all is gathered together.
